verdict.rationale: PostHog's own docs say its CLI is built for use from coding agents, local scripts, and CI/CD pipelines. The docs also say flag definitions can be managed from your own tooling and CI, and experiments can be managed programmatically. A published OpenAPI spec backs this headless, automation-oriented use. The documented CLI login is a browser-based flow, so non-interactive CI authentication is not shown, and there is no independent confirmation that CI usage works. Missing for 10: documented non-interactive/headless CLI authentication for CI (e.g., API key via environment variable), concrete CI pipeline examples, and independent or hands-on confirmation of CI automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: The PostHog CLI lets you use PostHog from your terminal, your coding agents, local scripts, and CI/CD pipelines.
Evaluate flags at runtime and manage flag definitions from your own tooling and CI.
Manage experiments, holdouts, and shared metrics programmatically from your own systems.
